To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a novel technology allowing us to generate large, highly diverse phage banks that can be used for the rapid and efficient detection and control of emerging bacterial pathogens.

we developed and tested a technology that allows the efficient and rapid production of large banks of genetically engineered phages, and that this technology is applicable to a wide variety of bacterial pathogens.
we have developed technologies to produce large, genetically engineered phage banks, which should allow us to detect, diagnose, and control emergent pathogenic bacterial strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a phage-based technology for the rapid and efficient detection and control of emerging bacterial pathogens.

the development of technologies that will enable us to rapidly produce, screen, and deploy genetically engineered phage-based banks for use in the detection and the control of emergent bacterial threats.
the development of a new generation of genetically engineered phage banks, with a wide spectrum of functions, for the detection, control, and eradication of emergent multidrug-resistant pathogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have created a new paradigm for the development of genetically engineered, highly virulent phage populations, which can be applied to a wide range of emergent pathogens, and that such phage banks can be used to rapidly detect and control such emergent threats.
we have developed a technology that can lead to the production of very diverse, large banks of genetically modified, virulent phages.
this technology provides a powerful tool for rapid, specific, and effective detection and control of bacterial pathogens, including those of bioterrorist concern.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for the first time, we have demonstrated the feasibility of creating and screening large banks of genetically engineered virulent phages, each carrying a unique genetic modification, to identify those that are able to detect and eradicate emergent bacterial pathogens.

, using a combination of molecular and genetic techniques and the T4 phage as a model system, we have demonstrated the feasibility of producing large, genetically engineered virulent phages banks, and have shown how such banks can be used to rapidly isolate phage variants capable of detecting (diagnosing) and destroying a wide range of gram-negative bacteria.

the development of such a technology would allow us to rapidly and simultaneously produce, in the laboratory, a large bank of genetically engineered phages capable of detecting, infecting, and killing a very wide range of bacterial species, and thus provide a rapid, highly efficient, and effective means to control emergent bacterial pathogens, including those that may be engineered as bioterrorism agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that

phage banks, which are genetically engineered to contain a very wide spectrum (ie, a very large number) of variants of a given gene, are a very powerful tool for the detection and control, within hours of infection, of emergent multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens, for which no effective antibiotics or vaccine exist.

phages can be engineered as a highly flexible and efficient means to detect, and then control, the spread of emergent pathogen threats, including those that are antibiotic-resistant and/or genetically engineered for use in bioterrorism.
the use of a genetically engineered phage bank, containing a wide spectrum of variants, can be used to rapidly detect emergent bacterial threats.
